title: Java Advanced Sorting
learningObjectives: Reverse a comparator without subtraction arithmetic.
Use stable sorting to preserve equal-key relative order.
Choose sorting rules that are deterministic and readable.

understand.concept: Advanced sorting combines Comparator factories and chained comparisons to order custom objects. Comparator.comparing selects a key, comparingInt and comparingDouble avoid unnecessary boxing, and thenComparing adds tie-breakers. reversed reverses the complete comparator built so far. Java's list sorting is stable, so elements that compare equal retain their prior relative order.
understand.whyItMatters: This topic equips Java learners to write robust programs using java advanced sorting in real applications.
understand.analogy: Think of each language feature as a clearly labelled tool: choose it for the specific problem it is designed to solve.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace the Java language and library contracts; compile and test the actual behaviour.

explain.narrative: Model the desired ordering explicitly: first compare by a primary property, then by secondary properties. Use nullsFirst or nullsLast when nullable keys are part of the data model. Do not compare integers by subtracting one from another because overflow can break comparator contracts; use Integer.compare. Sorting a list is in place, so copy first if the original order must be retained.

practise.guidedTask: Build a small Java program that demonstrates java advanced sorting. Predict the output before compiling with JDK 21.
practise.independentTask: Create a practical application using java advanced sorting. Include at least two test cases, expected output, and an explanation of one important edge case.
hints: Use Comparator.comparing to sort by a selected key and thenComparing to define deterministic tie-breakers.
Use reversed on the comparator to reverse its ordering; be clear whether only one key or the whole comparison is reversed.
Test equal keys, null values according to the chosen policy and stability when the same comparator is applied.
practise.challenge: Extend one example into a small reusable component and document its error handling, ordering or concurrency guarantees as relevant.

questions.prompt: Which method adds a secondary comparison?
questions.explanation: thenComparing applies a tie-breaker when the first comparator returns zero.
comparingInt builds a comparator using an int-valued key extractor.
reversed returns a comparator with the opposite ordering.

questions.answer: Null values sort after non-null values
